design: D1 The check is per launch, in the Hub, not in the judge. D2 Asked once per content; Deny is remembered until new operator input or new content. Migration 0133_workspace_fingerprints adds one table (PK project_id, workspace_key); nothing existing changes. Hazard: it reaches the operator's :8000 database on its next restart; after it every workspace's first launch records a baseline. Rollback: alembic downgrade 0132 drops the table and launches start unchecked.

checked: Acceptance test committed xfail(strict) at 9339833, passing after the build

problem: The workspace judge reads commands as text. F675 refuses writes to the runner's configuration it can see in a command's words, but the class is open by construction (git apply of a patch, git checkout, archive extraction, cd/Join-Path splits, a copy naming only the directory). An allow rule in .claude/settings.local.json runs ahead of --permission-prompt-tool on the next turn, and a hook runs with no check at all, so the boundary has to be structural: the Hub, which launches every turn, checks what the runner will read before it launches.

requirements.rationale: A text judge cannot see every way a turn can write the configuration the next turn's runner reads; the launch can.
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL fingerprint the runner-config paths (runner_config.RUNNER_CONFIG_PATHS: the existence and content hash of each file, directories enumerated) in the directory a turn starts in (agent checkout, task checkout, review checkout or project directory) before the turn starts, and compare it with the fingerprint recorded for that workspace; an unchanged fingerprint SHALL let the turn start.

requirements.rationale: An allow rule or hook written by a turn must not take effect before the operator has seen it.
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL hold a turn whose workspace's runner configuration differs from its record (no run is created, its queued input stays queued and uncounted, and its waiting_reason names the files) and SHALL ask the operator once per content on the permission surface, as a run-less permission request with tool_name RunnerConfiguration and tool_input.paths naming each changed file. Allow SHALL record the new fingerprint and re-drain the queue so the held turn starts; Deny SHALL keep the turn held and not ask again until new operator input arrives or the files change; restoring the files SHALL release the turn without an answer.

requirements.rationale: Without the second condition a reviewer's fresh checkout of an agent's commit to .claude/settings.json would be accepted silently.
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL record a workspace's first fingerprint silently when the workspace is the project directory, or when every runner-config file in it is one the project directory already holds unchanged; otherwise the first launch SHALL be asked about like a change.

requirements.rationale: mcp_server.py is spawned standalone and restates the list; the judge and the fingerprint must read one list.
requirements.statement: mcp_server._RUNNER_CONFIG_PATHS SHALL equal runner_config.RUNNER_CONFIG_PATHS, and a test SHALL pin them equal.

requirements.rationale: F676: a pipe can carry a path the judge never reads. F737 rider: py -3.11, py -V:3.12 and python -u read code from their input, and gc names.txt | Get-Item | Remove-Item takes its paths from a file.
requirements.statement: Under the Workspace posture the shell judge SHALL refuse a command whose stage takes paths or code from another command's output: xargs or parallel anywhere; after a pipe, a shell, eval or source, a while-read loop that does more than print, or an interpreter given no code of its own (options alone, or the py version selector); a decoder (base64 -d, xxd -r) feeding a pipe or a substitution; pwsh -EncodedCommand; and in PowerShell Invoke-Expression or iex, [scriptblock]::Create, FromBase64String, and a path cmdlet fed by a pipe (directly or in a ForEach-Object block using $_) unless a listing such as Get-ChildItem feeds it, where a pipe-fed listing does not exempt the stage after it. Reading stages (| wc, | head, | python -m json.tool) SHALL stay allowed.

in_scope: a held turn and its RunnerConfiguration permission request
mcp_server._decide pipe-fed interpreter and listing shapes
non_goals: A runner's own mid-turn hot-reload of its settings (the check is per launch)
Any Hub route writing these files

summary: Before every launch the Hub fingerprints the runner configuration in the turn's workspace and compares it with that workspace's last approved launch; a change holds the turn and asks the operator, naming the files (F737). Rider: pipe-fed interpreter and listing shapes in the shell judge.
title: A changed runner configuration holds the next turn
